one_liner: A senior attorney job at the Bureau of Prisons' Washington headquarters, advising leaders on correctional law, sentencing, First Step Act implementation, and proposed legislation.
fit_summary: This job requires a J.D. and active bar membership in any U.S. jurisdiction, and nothing on file shows Daniel has either. Daniel's policy knowledge and government-client consulting at IEM are relevant to the legislative-review part of the work. At GS-14/15, though, this is a practicing-attorney role, and without a law license Daniel cannot qualify.
eligibility: Required: a J.D. degree and active membership in the bar of any U.S. jurisdiction. Confirm Daniel holds both before applying.
Open to the public as an excepted-service attorney appointment (hiring paths listed: excepted, public, Peace Corps), so prior federal status is not needed.
U.S. citizenship and Selective Service registration (if applicable) are required.
Clearance is listed as 'Other'; see the Special Conditions of Employment, which likely include a background investigation.
Grade (GS-14 or 15) is set by the experience your resume and transcripts document. The posting prefers correctional law or litigation experience.
strategy: First confirm the hard requirement: if you do not have a J.D. and active bar membership, skip this posting, because Direct Hire still requires the basic qualification.
If you are a licensed attorney, state your bar jurisdiction, admission date, and active status at the top of your two-page resume.
Frame IEM work as advising government clients on statutes, regulations, and policy, using [your actual duties]. Highlight any legislative or policy analysis.
Spend most of the resume on legal experience (litigation, legal research, policy and legislative drafting), with hours per week and dates stated briefly.
Apply between Oct 25 and Nov 3, 2026, a 10-day window. Upload your transcripts and any bar certificate the announcement requests.
If you are not an attorney, search USAJOBS for BOP or DOJ legislative affairs, policy analyst (0101/0301), or emergency management (0089) roles instead.
resume_bullets: Advised [client/agency] on interpretation and compliance with [federal/state statutes and regulations], producing [memos/policy recommendations] for senior leaders.
Reviewed and analyzed [number] pieces of proposed legislation and internal policies for [organization], identifying impacts on [program/operations].
Coordinated with [federal/state/local] officials across [number] agencies to resolve [statutory/operational] issues during [project/disaster recovery effort].
interview_questions: How would you approach analyzing proposed legislation that affects BOP operations?
Describe your experience with federal sentencing, the First Step Act, or prisoners' rights issues.
Tell us about a time you gave legal advice to senior leaders who disagreed with your conclusion.
How do you manage tight deadlines across multiple agencies and stakeholders?
watch_outs: The J.D. and active bar membership are mandatory, and nothing on file shows Daniel meets them.
The application window is short (Oct 25 to Nov 3, 2026).
The job is on-site in Washington, DC with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
At GS-14/15, competitive applicants will likely have years of legal practice.
